questions.q: According to this lesson, what makes up a meaningful chunk of a real ServiceNow Administrator's week that a typical job posting undersells?
options: Reactive troubleshooting — access issues, misrouted approvals, and broken scheduled jobs that need a fast diagnosis
Writing marketing copy for the service catalog
Negotiating the company's ServiceNow licensing contract
Designing the company's physical network infrastructure
questions.explain: The job posting lists maintenance tasks, but a real admin seat spends significant time reacting to specific, often urgent platform issues.

questions.q: Which two earlier courses in this path does ongoing ACL, role, and group management draw on directly?
options: Course 5 (JavaScript for ServiceNow) and course 9 (CMDB/CSDM)
Course 3 (System Administration) and course 10 (Security & Access Controls)
Course 1 (ITSM/ITIL 4 Foundations) only
Course 13 (Technical Architecture) and course 14 (Career & Capstone)
questions.explain: The lesson ties recurring access-management work directly back to System Administration (course 3) and Security & Access Controls (course 10).

questions.q: What is the distinction the lesson draws between a platform ticket and an ITSM process ticket?
options: There is no real distinction — all tickets are handled identically
A platform ticket means the underlying platform itself is malfunctioning (a form, notification, or report); a process ticket is about a business issue within a working process
Platform tickets are always higher priority than process tickets
Process tickets are resolved by developers, never by administrators
questions.explain: Platform tickets are about the platform misbehaving; process tickets are about a business issue inside an otherwise-functioning process.

questions.q: What role do administrators typically play when an ITSM process owner wants a workflow change, per this lesson?
options: Administrators unilaterally redesign the process without consulting the process owner
Administrators have no involvement in ITSM process changes
Administrators translate the process owner's desired change into a correctly scoped configuration change, without breaking what already works
Administrators only escalate the request to ServiceNow support
questions.explain: The process owner owns the decision; the administrator's job is translating that decision into a safe, correctly scoped platform change.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say the "ServiceNow Administrator" title can mean different things at different companies?
options: The title is standardized by ServiceNow and means exactly the same thing everywhere
At smaller organizations it's often a hybrid admin/developer role; at larger enterprises it's more likely to be specialized and separate from development
Smaller companies never hire ServiceNow administrators
Larger enterprises always combine admin and architect responsibilities into one role
questions.explain: Company size strongly affects whether the role is a specialized, admin-only function or a hybrid that also includes development work.
